critical_concepts.elaboration: Two useful normalizations answer different questions. Relative bar range, 100 × (high − low) / close, compares a candle's size with the asset's price. Close location, (close − low) / (high − low), places the close from 0 (at the low) to 1 (at the high). The supplied indicator does not calculate either measure; they are useful companions for comparing candles and reading where a bar closed.

True Range is the largest of high − low, |high − previous close|, and |low − previous close|, so a gap from the previous close is included. ATR smooths True Range and measures movement size, not direction. This implementation uses Wilder's RMA: an initial simple-average seed followed by prior ATR + (current TR − prior ATR) / period.

ADX is a smoothed measure of trend strength. It does not tell whether the trend is up or down; the companion +DI and −DI lines provide directional context. ADX is not calculated in the supplied indicator, so it is presented as a possible regime filter rather than an existing signal input.

critical_concepts.concept: Swing Pivots and Classic Pivot Levels
critical_concepts.elaboration: A swing pivot high is a local high with lower highs around it; a swing pivot low is a local low with higher lows around it. A pivot needs bars after the candidate to confirm, so it is known with a delay. The code uses delayed swing pivots to compare price and oscillator extremes for divergence. Classic daily/weekly pivot levels are separate support/resistance calculations and are not used here.

Clustering is an unsupervised learning task: it groups observations by similarity without pre-labeled answers. The indicator uses ATR observations as its input and asks whether current volatility is closest to a low, middle, or high-volatility group. Those labels describe the recent training window, not fixed market truths.

K-means alternates between assigning each value to its nearest center and moving each center to the mean of its assigned values. The supplied helper runs one-dimensional K-means with three ordered centers. For each bar, it fits centers using earlier ATR values, assigns the current ATR to the nearest center, and blends the ATR with that center to create an adaptive ATR.

The implementation combines Wilder-smoothed ATR, three K-means volatility regimes, ATR-scaled Supertrend bands, a centered momentum oscillator, and pivot-based divergence. A buy or sell flag is only considered after trend confirmation and readiness checks, then filtered by volatility, shock size, entry distance, momentum, and opposing divergence.

interactive_questions.prompt: Trace how OHLC bars become volatility features and why a swing pivot is confirmed later.
interactive_questions.question: Follow the source logic from True Range through ATR and the historical volatility clusters.
interactive_questions.explanation: ATR measures the size of movement. Past ATR values set the three cluster centers, and the current ATR is assigned to its nearest center. The pivot index is shifted back by pivot_len so a local extreme is used only after right-side bars have arrived.
interactive_questions.codeSnippet:
previous_close = np.r_[close[0], close[:-1]]
true_range = np.maximum.reduce([
    high - low,
    np.abs(high - previous_close),
    np.abs(low - previous_close),
])
atr = _rma(true_range, atr_period)

# A candidate swing point is checked only after right-side bars arrive.
pivot = i - pivot_len

# Fit centers on earlier ATR values, then classify the current ATR.
window = atr[i - training_period:i]
centers, _, converged, _ = _kmeans3(window, centroid_seeds, max_iter)
regime = int(np.abs(centers - atr[i]).argmin())
adaptive_atr = (1.0 - centroid_weight) * atr[i] + centroid_weight * centers[regime]

steps.title: True Range Includes Gaps
steps.description: The bar's range is compared with both distances from the previous close. The largest value captures the full movement even when price opens beyond the prior close.

mcq.question: Why does True Range compare the current high and low with the previous close?

options.text: To account for a gap from the previous close.
options.reasoning: A gap can make the true movement larger than the current high minus low.

options.text: To identify whether the candle closed bullish.
options.reasoning: True Range is non-directional and measures movement size.

steps.title: ATR Smooths Movement Size
steps.description: The source calls _rma on True Range. Its Wilder average reacts to new movement while retaining information from earlier bars. ATR is a distance in price units, not a forecast of up or down.

steps.title: Swing Pivots Need Confirmation
steps.description: The candidate is pivot_len bars behind the current bar. Those bars to its right must be available before the code can decide that the candidate is a local high or low. The result is delayed confirmation, not a pivot known at the candidate bar in real time.

steps.title: Cluster Historical Volatility
steps.description: The window ends before the current index. K-means learns three centers from recent ATR values; the current ATR is then mapped to the nearest center and blended with that center to form adaptive_atr.

mcq.question: What does the cluster number describe here?

options.text: A recent low, middle, or high ATR regime.
options.reasoning: The clusters are learned from ATR values and sorted by center.

options.text: A guaranteed prediction that price will rise or fall.
options.reasoning: The feature being clustered is volatility, which has no direction.

steps.title: Scale Bands to Recent Volatility
steps.description: The midpoint anchors the bands and adaptive_atr sets their distance. A larger volatility regime widens the initial band distance; the multiplier controls that distance.

steps.title: Trail the Active Bands
steps.description: The upper band can ratchet downward and the lower band can ratchet upward, unless price has crossed the previous band. This state carries across bars.

steps.title: Flip and Confirm
steps.description: A close through the opposite active band flips direction. direction_run then counts consecutive bars in that direction; until it reaches confirmation_bars, the output is zero (wait).

steps.title: Fit on the Past, Classify the Present
steps.description: Python's stop-exclusive slice ends at i, so the current bar is not used to fit centers that will classify itself. This avoids one form of look-ahead in the volatility model.

steps.title: Reject Oversized Shocks
steps.description: The ratio compares current True Range with the prior ATR. If the move is too large relative to recent movement, the filter can skip a signal instead of entering after a shock bar.

steps.title: Bound Stop Distance
steps.description: Risk is the close-to-band distance in the active direction. The ATR cap makes the maximum accepted distance scale with recent volatility.

steps.title: Gate the Entry, Then Test Execution
steps.description: A valid entry must pass the non-directional guards and agree with trend and momentum. A backtest should timestamp the decision at the bar close and model the next executable price, costs, and slippage.
